newsitem.title: LIBERIA: Liberia's Taylor disbands artillery division.
newsitem.headline: Liberia's Taylor disbands artillery division.

text.p: The head of Liberia's largest faction, Charles Taylor, disbanded a 1,500-fighter artillery division in his Gbarnga headquarters on Saturday less than a week before a deadline for militia fighters to disarm.

Taylor's National Patriotic Front of Liberia handed over U.S.-made howitzers, anti-aircraft and multi-barrelled guns, long-range mortars and surface-to-surface missiles, peacekeepers and U.N. monitors said.
The deadline for disarmament, part of a deal brokered by West African leaders last August, expires on January 31.
Nigerian-led peacekeepers and West African foreign ministers had deplored the slow pace of disarmament and the quality of weapons being handed over.
Last week less than 9,000 of the estimated 60,000 fighters had demobilised but monitors said on Saturday that the process was showing signs of gathering pace.
The heads of state have threatened sanctions against any warlord derailing the peace deal, the latest in a long line.
Taylor, who launched Liberia's civil war in 1989, says he plans to contest presidential elections in May.
Freed American slaves set up Liberia in 1847. The civil war has killed well over 150,000 people.
